# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1125
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1125
- **Title**: fix(#1121): transparent bounded retry on zero-byte connect-stall watchdog timeout
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1121` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +1023
- **Deletions**: -37
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T20:11:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T20:13:48Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1121

## Root cause

`httpClient.send` completes only when the response **headers** arrive, so the connect watchdog's `TimeoutException` in `_sendWatched` (lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart) means **zero response bytes** — the provider never started generating. That exception escalated straight to the adapter's error event → run aborted. Bench run 36742787166 (glm-5.3-flash) lost 3/38 tasks this way (`gpt2-codegolf`, `polyglot-rust-c`, `write-compressor`): first request stalled on connect, watchdog fired at ~171s, `aborted: Request was aborted`, task scored failed with the prompt never sent.

## Retry semantics

- **Where:** `_sendWatched` — the single choke point all streaming adapters route through (`startProviderResponse` → `sendProviderRequest`). A connect-watchdog `TimeoutException` is retried **in place**, below the roles failover ladder and below `TransientRetryStream`.
- **Budget:** `providerConnectRetries = 2` (3 total attempts), backoff `providerConnectRetryBackoff` doubling 1s → 2s. Worst case ≈ 3×(180s+backoff) ≈ 10 min — the unattended/bench tradeoff priced in the issue (E1). Separate budget: a network stall never consumes a `retriesPerEntry` failover attempt (#1066 semantics) and never burns a `TransientRetryStream` attempt.
- **Safety:** zero bytes received ⇒ no partial stream to corrupt, no committed state, nothing double-billed (a request the endpoint never answered is not a billed generation) — the identical payload is simply re-sent. Retries ride a fresh `http.Request` clone via the existing `_reissue` helper (a sent Request is finalized by the client and not re-sendable — the redirect path clones for the same reason; this bug class is pinned by the #1036 MockClient test).
- **Observable, no new telemetry:** each retry fires the existing `transientRetryNotice` hook — the CLI host prints its dim `[net]` line + writes fa.log; hosts that leave the hook null (app host) stay silent, same as mid-stream retries today.
- **Exhaustion:** the same named watchdog `TimeoutException` rethrows unchanged → `formatProviderError` renders the `TimeoutException:` keyword → the roles/queue classifiers fail over exactly as today; a hard-down endpoint still dies loudly.
- **Mid-stream unchanged (AC3):** idle-timeout silence fires downstream in `createSseIterator` and never re-enters this layer — byte-identical path, pinned by test.
- **User abort:** the retry sleeper races the cancel token; a cancel during backoff propagates the abort (E4).

## Bench incident class coverage

The exact incident shape — first provider request stalled into the watchdog → run death — now survives up to 2 transparent retries with a visible note; a recovering endpoint answers on attempt 2/3 and the task proceeds. UT-1/UT-2/UT-3 (issue ACs) covered in `test/providers/connect_stall_retry_test.dart` (fake stream, 20ms watchdog, injectable sleeper): retry-to-success, exhaust→same error, mid-stream NOT retried, cancel-mid-backoff, happy path untouched. Scoped analyze clean; `test/providers` + `test/model_roles` suites green (722 tests).

Built on ai/gh-1036 (#1108, approved) — merged into this branch because #1036 review-round-2 reshaped `_sendWatched` itself; no conflict when that lands.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs

Before this PR: `await for (... ) { cancelToken?.throwIfCancelled(); ... }` — same delayed-cancel behavior (only checks between lines). And there was no watchdog at all, so a hang was forever. So not a regression — but now that they built the consumption loop, they could wire the cancelToken like createSseIterator does. It's a parity gap: createSseIterator supports cancelToken natively; `_consumeSseLines` reimplements a degraded version. SUGGESTION-level.

2. `_request` — the timeout on `client.send` — the 401-refresh loop and Cloudflare loop re-request; each gets its own 180s connect budget. Fine.

Is codex supposed to be covered by #1121? The issue says bench run lost 3/38 tasks — glm-5.3-flash — that routes through the standard adapters (openai-like), not codex. The retry is placed in `_sendWatched` "the single choke point all streaming adapters route through" — but codex does NOT route through it (has own client.send). This is an inconsistency: the codex adapter got a watchdog but no connect-stall retry, while all others retry. Given #1121's motivation (bench reliability), codex sessions (chatgpt codex backend) won't benefit. Worth flagging as IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION? It's a coverage gap vs the PR's stated goal ("the single choke point all streaming adapters route through" — inaccurate claim since codex bypasses). I'd flag as SUGGESTION (documented inconsistency) or IMPORTANT. Errors on the original future after timeout ARE swallowed (the internal listener handles them). Yes — `_future.timeout` chains `.then((v) { if (timer.isActive) ... }, onError: ...)` — the implementation registers handlers on the source future, so late errors are not uncaught. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1125
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1125
- **Title**: fix(#1121): transparent bounded retry on zero-byte connect-stall watchdog timeout
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1121` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +1023
- **Deletions**: -37
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T20:11:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T20:13:48Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1121

## Root cause

`httpClient.send` completes only when the response **headers** arrive, so the connect watchdog's `TimeoutException` in `_sendWatched` (lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart) means **zero response bytes** — the provider never started generating. That exception escalated straight to the adapter's error event → run aborted. Bench run 36742787166 (glm-5.3-flash) lost 3/38 tasks this way (`gpt2-codegolf`, `polyglot-rust-c`, `write-compressor`): first request stalled on connect, watchdog fired at ~171s, `aborted: Request was aborted`, task scored failed with the prompt never sent.

## Retry semantics

- **Where:** `_sendWatched` — the single choke point all streaming adapters route through (`startProviderResponse` → `sendProviderRequest`). A connect-watchdog `TimeoutException` is retried **in place**, below the roles failover ladder and below `TransientRetryStream`.
- **Budget:** `providerConnectRetries = 2` (3 total attempts), backoff `providerConnectRetryBackoff` doubling 1s → 2s. Worst case ≈ 3×(180s+backoff) ≈ 10 min — the unattended/bench tradeoff priced in the issue (E1). Separate budget: a network stall never consumes a `retriesPerEntry` failover attempt (#1066 semantics) and never burns a `TransientRetryStream` attempt.
- **Safety:** zero bytes received ⇒ no partial stream to corrupt, no committed state, nothing double-billed (a request the endpoint never answered is not a billed generation) — the identical payload is simply re-sent. Retries ride a fresh `http.Request` clone via the existing `_reissue` helper (a sent Request is finalized by the client and not re-sendable — the redirect path clones for the same reason; this bug class is pinned by the #1036 MockClient test).
- **Observable, no new telemetry:** each retry fires the existing `transientRetryNotice` hook — the CLI host prints its dim `[net]` line + writes fa.log; hosts that leave the hook null (app host) stay silent, same as mid-stream retries today.
- **Exhaustion:** the same named watchdog `TimeoutException` rethrows unchanged → `formatProviderError` renders the `TimeoutException:` keyword → the roles/queue classifiers fail over exactly as today; a hard-down endpoint still dies loudly.
- **Mid-stream unchanged (AC3):** idle-timeout silence fires downstream in `createSseIterator` and never re-enters this layer — byte-identical path, pinned by test.
- **User abort:** the retry sleeper races the cancel token; a cancel during backoff propagates the abort (E4).

## Bench incident class coverage

The exact incident shape — first provider request stalled into the watchdog → run death — now survives up to 2 transparent retries with a visible note; a recovering endpoint answers on attempt 2/3 and the task proceeds. # pr-1125: fix(#1121): transparent bounded retry on zero-byte connect-stall watchdog timeout

## Description

Fixes #1121

## Root cause

`httpClient.send` completes only when the response **headers** arrive, so the connect watchdog's `TimeoutException` in `_sendWatched` (lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart) means **zero response bytes** — the provider never started generating. That exception escalated straight to the adapter's error event → run aborted. Bench run 36742787166 (glm-5.3-flash) lost 3/38 tasks this way (`gpt2-codegolf`, `polyglot-rust-c`, `write-compressor`): first request stalled on connect, watchdog fired at ~171s, `aborted: Request was aborted`, task scored failed with the prompt never sent.

## Retry semantics

- **Where:** `_sendWatched` — the single choke point all streaming adapters route through (`startProviderResponse` → `sendProviderRequest`). A connect-watchdog `TimeoutException` is retried **in place**, below the roles failover ladder and below `TransientRetryStream`.
- **Budget:** `providerConnectRetries = 2` (3 total attempts), backoff `providerConnectRetryBackoff` doubling 1s → 2s. Worst case ≈ 3×(180s+backoff) ≈ 10 min — the unattended/bench tradeoff priced in the issue (E1). Separate budget: a network stall never consumes a `retriesPerEntry` failover attempt (#1066 semantics) and never burns a `TransientRetryStream` attempt.
- **Safety:** zero bytes received ⇒ no partial stream to corrupt, no committed state, nothing double-billed (a request the endpoint never answered is not a billed generation) — the identical payload is simply re-sent. Retries ride a fresh `http.Request` clone via the existing `_reissue` helper (a sent Request is finalized by the client and not re-sendable — the redirect path clones for the same reason; this bug class is pinned by the #1036 MockClient test).
- **Observable, no new telemetry:** each retry fires the existing `transientRetryNotice` hook — the CLI host prints its dim `[net]` line + writes fa.log; hosts that leave the hook null (app host) stay silent, same as mid-stream retries today.
- **Exhaustion:** the same named watchdog `TimeoutException` rethrows unchanged → `formatProviderError` renders the `TimeoutException:` keyword → the roles/queue classifiers fail over exactly as today; a hard-down endpoint still dies loudly.
- **Mid-stream unchanged (AC3):** idle-timeout silence fires downstream in `createSseIterator` and never re-enters this layer — byte-identical path, pinned by test.
- **User abort:** the retry sleeper races the cancel token; a cancel during backoff propagates the abort (E4).

## Bench incident class coverage

The exact incident shape — first provider request stalled into the watchdog → run death — now survives up to 2 transparent retries with a visible note; a recovering endpoint answers on attempt 2/3 and the task proceeds. UT-1/UT-2/UT-3 (issue ACs) covered in `test/providers/connect_stall_retry_test.dart` (fake stream, 20ms watchdog, injectable sleeper): retry-to-success, exhaust→same error, mid-stream NOT retried, cancel-mid-backoff, happy path untouched. Scoped analyze clean; `test/providers` + `test/model_roles` suites green (722 tests).

Built on ai/gh-1036 (#1108, approved) — merged into this branch because #1036 review-round-2 reshaped `_sendWatched` itself; no conflict when that lands.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap

Interesting details in `chatgpt_codex.dart`:

1. `_consumeSseLines` — no `cancelToken` wiring into the stream itself: cancel during silence is only noticed at the next line or at idle timeout. `createSseIterator` DOES wire the cancel token (abandon + cancel immediately). So codex loses prompt-cancel latency during silence: a user abort during a silent codex stream waits up to `streamIdle` (5 min default) to take effect. Pre-existing? Before this PR: `await for (... ) { cancelToken?.throwIfCancelled(); ... }` — same delayed-cancel behavior (only checks between lines). And there was no watchdog at all, so a hang was forever. So not a regression — but now that they built the consumption loop, they could wire the cancelToken like createSseIterator does. It's a parity gap: createSseIterator supports cancelToken natively; `_consumeSseLines` reimplements a degraded version. SUGGESTION-level.

2. `_request` — the timeout on `client.send` — the 401-refresh loop and Cloudflare loop re-request; each gets its own 180s connect budget. Fine.

3. Note: in `run()`, after `_consumeSseLines`, `_sse.finish(_handleEvent)` etc. If `_consumeSseLines` throws TimeoutException, it propagates out of run() — presumably caught by the adapter's try/catch turning into ErrorEvent. The test confirms ErrorEvent. Good.

4. Codex connect watchdog: uses `effectiveProviderConnectTimeout` (streaming budget, 180s) — consistent with _sendWatched. BUT — no retry for codex! The #1121 retry only applies to `_sendWatched` (sendProviderRequest). Codex has its own `_request` path (bypasses sendProviderRequest) — so codex's connect stall does NOT retry. Is codex supposed to be covered by #1121? The issue says bench run lost 3/38 tasks — glm-5.3-flash — that routes through the standard adapters (openai-like), not codex. The retry is placed in `_sendWatched` "the single choke point all streaming adapters route through" — but codex does NOT route through it (has own client.send). This is an inconsistency: the codex adapter got a watchdog but no connect-stall retry, while all others retry. Given #1121's motivation (bench reliability), codex sessions (chatgpt codex backend) won't benefit. Worth flagging as IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION? It's a coverage gap vs the PR's stated goal ("the single choke point all streaming adapters route through" — inaccurate claim since codex bypasses). I'd flag as SUGGESTION (documented inconsistency) or IMPORTANT. Let me check which adapters route through sendProviderRequest — anthropic, openai-completions, etc. Let me verify codex is the only bypass.

Also check `copilot` adapter, `dial`, etc. — do they use sendProviderRequest? Let me grep.

So for codex, a user abort during a wedged connect waits the full 180s watchdog (abort not honored) — previously it waited forever; now 180s. createSseIterator/_sendWatchedOnce both race the cancel token. Parity gap again — same family as the _consumeSseLines cancel gap. The session has a cancelToken (used in _consumeSseLines). So a user abort during a codex connect-stall is not honored until the watchdog fires. SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? User-facing responsiveness... I'd say SUGGESTION (edge case; bounded now).

But since the PR touches exactly this line to add the watchdog, adding the cancel race would have been cheap. SUGGESTION.

A >180s header wait means the request is queued/stuck server-side (or network wedge) — unlikely to be billing generation. But a leak of the abandoned socket per attempt is real. Errors on the original future after timeout ARE swallowed (the internal listener handles them). Good, no uncaught-error hazard.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1125
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1125
- **Title**: fix(#1121): transparent bounded retry on zero-byte connect-stall watchdog timeout
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1121` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +1023
- **Deletions**: -37
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T20:11:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T20:13:48Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1121

## Root cause

`httpClient.send` completes only when the response **headers** arrive, so the connect watchdog's `TimeoutException` in `_sendWatched` (lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart) means **zero response bytes** — the provider never started generating. That exception escalated straight to the adapter's error event → run aborted. Bench run 36742787166 (glm-5.3-flash) lost 3/38 tasks this way (`gpt2-codegolf`, `polyglot-rust-c`, `write-compressor`): first request stalled on connect, watchdog fired at ~171s, `aborted: Request was aborted`, task scored failed with the prompt never sent.

## Retry semantics

- **Where:** `_sendWatched` — the single choke point all streaming adapters route through (`startProviderResponse` → `sendProviderRequest`). A connect-watchdog `TimeoutException` is retried **in place**, below the roles failover ladder and below `TransientRetryStream`.
- **Budget:** `providerConnectRetries = 2` (3 total attempts), backoff `providerConnectRetryBackoff` doubling 1s → 2s. Worst case ≈ 3×(180s+backoff) ≈ 10 min — the unattended/bench tradeoff priced in the issue (E1). Separate budget: a network stall never consumes a `retriesPerEntry` failover attempt (#1066 semantics) and never burns a `TransientRetryStream` attempt.
- **Safety:** zero bytes received ⇒ no partial stream to corrupt, no committed state, nothing double-billed (a request the endpoint never answered is not a billed generation) — the identical payload is simply re-sent. Retries ride a fresh `http.Request` clone via the existing `_reissue` helper (a sent Request is finalized by the client and not re-sendable — the redirect path clones for the same reason; this bug class is pinned by the #1036 MockClient test).
- **Observable, no new telemetry:** each retry fires the existing `transientRetryNotice` hook — the CLI host prints its dim `[net]` line + writes fa.log; hosts that leave the hook null (app host) stay silent, same as mid-stream retries today.
- **Exhaustion:** the same named watchdog `TimeoutException` rethrows unchanged → `formatProviderError` renders the `TimeoutException:` keyword → the roles/queue classifiers fail over exactly as today; a hard-down endpoint still dies loudly.
- **Mid-stream unchanged (AC3):** idle-timeout silence fires downstream in `createSseIterator` and never re-enters this layer — byte-identical path, pinned by test.
- **User abort:** the retry sleeper races the cancel token; a cancel during backoff propagates the abort (E4).

## Bench incident class coverage

The exact incident shape — first provider request stalled into the watchdog → run death — now survives up to 2 transparent retries with a visible note; a recovering endpoint answers on attempt 2/3 and the task proceeds. UT-1/UT-2/UT-3 (issue ACs) covered in `test/providers/connect_stall_retry_test.dart` (fake stream, 20ms watchdog, injectable sleeper): retry-to-success, exhaust→same error, mid-stream NOT retried, cancel-mid-backoff, happy path untouched. Scoped analyze clean; `test/providers` + `test/model_roles` suites green (722 tests).

# pr-1125: fix(#1121): transparent bounded retry on zero-byte connect-stall watchdog timeout

## Description

Fixes #1121

## Root cause

`httpClient.send` completes only when the response **headers** arrive, so the connect watchdog's `TimeoutException` in `_sendWatched` (lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart) means **zero response bytes** — the provider never started generating. That exception escalated straight to the adapter's error event → run aborted. Bench run 36742787166 (glm-5.3-flash) lost 3/38 tasks this way (`gpt2-codegolf`, `polyglot-rust-c`, `write-compressor`): first request stalled on connect, watchdog fired at ~171s, `aborted: Request was aborted`, task scored failed with the prompt never sent.

## Retry semantics

- **Where:** `_sendWatched` — the single choke point all streaming adapters route through (`startProviderResponse` → `sendProviderRequest`). A connect-watchdog `TimeoutException` is retried **in place**, below the roles failover ladder and below `TransientRetryStream`.
- **Budget:** `providerConnectRetries = 2` (3 total attempts), backoff `providerConnectRetryBackoff` doubling 1s → 2s. Worst case ≈ 3×(180s+backoff) ≈ 10 min — the unattended/bench tradeoff priced in the issue (E1). Separate budget: a network stall never consumes a `retriesPerEntry` failover attempt (#1066 semantics) and never burns a `TransientRetryStream` attempt.
- **Safety:** zero bytes received ⇒ no partial stream to corrupt, no committed state, nothing double-billed (a request the endpoint never answered is not a billed generation) — the identical payload is simply re-sent. Retries ride a fresh `http.Request` clone via the existing `_reissue` helper (a sent Request is finalized by the client and not re-sendable — the redirect path clones for the same reason; this bug class is pinned by the #1036 MockClient test).
- **Observable, no new telemetry:** each retry fires the existing `transientRetryNotice` hook — the CLI host prints its dim `[net]` line + writes fa.log; hosts that leave the hook null (app host) stay silent, same as mid-stream retries today.
- **Exhaustion:** the same named watchdog `TimeoutException` rethrows unchanged → `formatProviderError` renders the `TimeoutException:` keyword → the roles/queue classifiers fail over exactly as today; a hard-down endpoint still dies loudly.
- **Mid-stream unchanged (AC3):** idle-timeout silence fires downstream in `createSseIterator` and never re-enters this layer — byte-identical path, pinned by test.
- **User abort:** the retry sleeper races the cancel token; a cancel during backoff propagates the abort (E4).

## Bench incident class coverage

The exact incident shape — first provider request stalled into the watchdog → run death — now survives up to 2 transparent retries with a visible note; a recovering endpoint answers on attempt 2/3 and the task proceeds. UT-1/UT-2/UT-3 (issue ACs) covered in `test/providers/connect_stall_retry_test.dart` (fake stream, 20ms watchdog, injectable sleeper): retry-to-success, exhaust→same error, mid-stream NOT retried, cancel-mid-backoff, happy path untouched. Scoped analyze clean; `test/providers` + `test/model_roles` suites green (722 tests).

Built on ai/gh-1036 (#1108, approved) — merged into this branch because #1036 review-round-2 reshaped `_sendWatched` itself; no conflict when that lands.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1125
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1125
- **Title**: fix(#1121): transparent bounded retry on zero-byte connect-stall watchdog timeout
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1121` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +1023
- **Deletions**: -37
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T20:11:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T20:13:48Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1121

## Root cause

`httpClient.send` completes only when the response **headers** arrive, so the connect watchdog's `TimeoutException` in `_sendWatched` (lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart) means **zero response bytes** — the provider never started generating. That exception escalated straight to the adapter's error event → run aborted. Bench run 36742787166 (glm-5.3-flash) lost 3/38 tasks this way (`gpt2-codegolf`, `polyglot-rust-c`, `write-compressor`): first request stalled on connect, watchdog fired at ~171s, `aborted: Request was aborted`, task scored failed with the prompt never sent.

## Retry semantics

- **Where:** `_sendWatched` — the single choke point all streaming adapters route through (`startProviderResponse` → `sendProviderRequest`). A connect-watchdog `TimeoutException` is retried **in place**, below the roles failover ladder and below `TransientRetryStream`.
- **Budget:** `providerConnectRetries = 2` (3 total attempts), backoff `providerConnectRetryBackoff` doubling 1s → 2s. Worst case ≈ 3×(180s+backoff) ≈ 10 min — the unattended/bench tradeoff priced in the issue (E1). Separate budget: a network stall never consumes a `retriesPerEntry` failover attempt (#1066 semantics) and never burns a `TransientRetryStream` attempt.
- **Safety:** zero bytes received ⇒ no partial stream to corrupt, no committed state, nothing double-billed (a request the endpoint never answered is not a billed generation) — the identical payload is simply re-sent. Retries ride a fresh `http.Request` clone via the existing `_reissue` helper (a sent Request is finalized by the client and not re-sendable — the redirect path clones for the same reason; this bug class is pinned by the #1036 MockClient test).
- **Observable, no new telemetry:** each retry fires the existing `transientRetryNotice` hook — the CLI host prints its dim `[net]` line + writes fa.log; hosts that leave the hook null (app host) stay silent, same as mid-stream retries today.
- **Exhaustion:** the same named watchdog `TimeoutException` rethrows unchanged → `formatProviderError` renders the `TimeoutException:` keyword → the roles/queue classifiers fail over exactly as today; a hard-down endpoint still dies loudly.
- **Mid-stream unchanged (AC3):** idle-timeout silence fires downstream in `createSseIterator` and never re-enters this layer — byte-identical path, pinned by test.
- **User abort:** the retry sleeper races the cancel token; a cancel during backoff propagates the abort (E4).

## Bench incident class coverage

The exact incident shape — first provider request stalled into the watchdog → run death — now survives up to 2 transparent retries with a visible note; a recovering endpoint answers on attempt 2/3 and the task proceeds. UT-1/UT-2/UT-3 (issue ACs) covered in `test/providers/connect_stall_retry_test.dart` (fake stream, 20ms watchdog, injectable sleeper): retry-to-success, exhaust→same error, mid-stream NOT retried, cancel-mid-backoff, happy path untouched. Scoped analyze clean; `test/providers` + `test/model_roles` suites green (722 tests).

Built on ai/gh-1036 (#1108, approved) — merged into this branch because #1036 review-round-2 reshaped `_sendWatched` itself; no conflict when that lands.

That exception escalated straight to the adapter's error event → run aborted. Bench run 36742787166 (glm-5.3-flash) lost 3/38 tasks this way (`gpt2-codegolf`, `polyglot-rust-c`, `write-compressor`): first request stalled on connect, watchdog fired at ~171s, `aborted: Request was aborted`, task scored failed with the prompt never sent.

## Retry semantics

- **Where:** `_sendWatched` — the single choke point all streaming adapters route through (`startProviderResponse` → `sendProviderRequest`). A connect-watchdog `TimeoutException` is retried **in place**, below the roles failover ladder and below `TransientRetryStream`.
- **Budget:** `providerConnectRetries = 2` (3 total attempts), backoff `providerConnectRetryBackoff` doubling 1s → 2s. Worst case ≈ 3×(180s+backoff) ≈ 10 min — the unattended/bench tradeoff priced in the issue (E1). Separate budget: a network stall never consumes a `retriesPerEntry` failover attempt (#1066 semantics) and never burns a `TransientRetryStream` attempt.
- **Safety:** zero bytes received ⇒ no partial stream to corrupt, no committed state, nothing double-billed (a request the endpoint never answered is not a billed generation) — the identical payload is simply re-sent. Retries ride a fresh `http.Request` clone via the existing `_reissue` helper (a sent Request is finalized by the client and not re-sendable — the redirect path clones for the same reason; this bug class is pinned by the #1036 MockClient test).
- **Observable, no new telemetry:** each retry fires the existing `transientRetryNotice` hook — the CLI host prints its dim `[net]` line + writes fa.log; hosts that leave the hook null (app host) stay silent, same as mid-stream retries today.
- **Exhaustion:** the same named watchdog `TimeoutException` rethrows unchanged → `formatProviderError` renders the `TimeoutException:` keyword → the roles/queue classifiers fail over exactly as today; a hard-down endpoint still dies loudly.
- **Mid-stream unchanged (AC3):** idle-timeout silence fires downstream in `createSseIterator` and never re-enters this layer — byte-identical path, pinned by test.
- **User abort:** the retry sleeper races the cancel token; a cancel during backoff propagates the abort (E4).

## Bench incident class coverage

The exact incident shape — first provider request stalled into the watchdog → run death — now survives up to 2 transparent retries with a visible note; a recovering endpoint answers on attempt 2/3 and the task proceeds. UT-1/UT-2/UT-3 (issue ACs) covered in `test/providers/connect_stall_retry_test.dart` (fake stream, 20ms watchdog, injectable sleeper): retry-to-success, exhaust→same error, mid-stream NOT retried, cancel-mid-backoff, happy path untouched. Scoped analyze clean; `test/providers` + `test/model_roles` suites green (722 tests).

Built on ai/gh-1036 (#1108, approved) — merged into this branch because #1036 review-round-2 reshaped `_sendWatched` itself; no conflict when that lands.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,

Interesting details in `chatgpt_codex.dart`:

1. `_consumeSseLines` — no `cancelToken` wiring into the stream itself: cancel during silence is only noticed at the next line or at idle timeout. `createSseIterator` DOES wire the cancel token (abandon + cancel immediately). So codex loses prompt-cancel latency during silence: a user abort during a silent codex stream waits up to `streamIdle` (5 min default) to take effect. Pre-existing? Before this PR: `await for (... ) { cancelToken?.throwIfCancelled(); ... }` — same delayed-cancel behavior (only checks between lines). And there was no watchdog at all, so a hang was forever. So not a regression — but now that they built the consumption loop, they could wire the cancelToken like createSseIterator does. It's a parity gap: createSseIterator supports cancelToken natively; `_consumeSseLines` reimplements a degraded version. SUGGESTION-level.

2. `_request` — the timeout on `client.send` — the 401-refresh loop and Cloudflare loop re-request; each gets its own 180s connect budget. Fine.

3. Note: in `run()`, after `_consumeSseLines`, `_sse.finish(_handleEvent)` etc. If `_consumeSseLines` throws TimeoutException, it propagates out of run() — presumably caught by the adapter's try/catch turning into ErrorEvent. The test confirms ErrorEvent. Good.

4. Codex connect watchdog: uses `effectiveProviderConnectTimeout` (streaming budget, 180s) — consistent with _sendWatched. BUT — no retry for codex! The #1121 retry only applies to `_sendWatched` (sendProviderRequest). Codex has its own `_request` path (bypasses sendProviderRequest) — so codex's connect stall does NOT retry. Is codex supposed to be covered by #1121? The issue says bench run lost 3/38 tasks — glm-5.3-flash — that routes through the standard adapters (openai-like), not codex. The retry is placed in `_sendWatched` "the single choke point all streaming adapters route through" — but codex does NOT route through it (has own client.send). This is an inconsistency: the codex adapter got a watchdog but no connect-stall retry, while all others retry. Given #1121's motivation (bench reliability), codex sessions (chatgpt codex backend) won't benefit. Worth flagging as IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION? It's a coverage gap vs the PR's stated goal ("the single choke point all streaming adapters route through" — inaccurate claim since codex bypasses). I'd flag as SUGGESTION (documented inconsistency) or IMPORTANT. Let me check which adapters route through sendProviderRequest — anthropic, openai-completions, etc. Let me verify codex is the only bypass.

Also check `copilot` adapter, `dial`, etc. — do they use sendProviderRequest? Let me grep.

5. The `chatgpt_codex` connect watchdog does NOT have the cancel token race! Look at `_request`: `client.send(request).timeout(...)` — no `Future.any` with cancelToken.onCancel. So for codex, a user abort during a wedged connect waits the full 180s watchdog (abort not honored) — previously it waited forever; now 180s. createSseIterator/_sendWatchedOnce both race the cancel token. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1125
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1125
- **Title**: fix(#1121): transparent bounded retry on zero-byte connect-stall watchdog timeout
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1121` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +1023
- **Deletions**: -37
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T20:11:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T20:13:48Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1121

## Root cause

`httpClient.send` completes only when the response **headers** arrive, so the connect watchdog's `TimeoutException` in `_sendWatched` (lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart) means **zero response bytes** — the provider never started generating. That exception escalated straight to the adapter's error event → run aborted. Bench run 36742787166 (glm-5.3-flash) lost 3/38 tasks this way (`gpt2-codegolf`, `polyglot-rust-c`, `write-compressor`): first request stalled on connect, watchdog fired at ~171s, `aborted: Request was aborted`, task scored failed with the prompt never sent.

## Retry semantics

- **Where:** `_sendWatched` — the single choke point all streaming adapters route through (`startProviderResponse` → `sendProviderRequest`). A connect-watchdog `TimeoutException` is retried **in place**, below the roles failover ladder and below `TransientRetryStream`.
- **Budget:** `providerConnectRetries = 2` (3 total attempts), backoff `providerConnectRetryBackoff` doubling 1s → 2s. Worst case ≈ 3×(180s+backoff) ≈ 10 min — the unattended/bench tradeoff priced in the issue (E1). Separate budget: a network stall never consumes a `retriesPerEntry` failover attempt (#1066 semantics) and never burns a `TransientRetryStream` attempt.
- **Safety:** zero bytes received ⇒ no partial stream to corrupt, no committed state, nothing double-billed (a request the endpoint never answered is not a billed generation) — the identical payload is simply re-sent. Retries ride a fresh `http.Request` clone via the existing `_reissue` helper (a sent Request is finalized by the client and not re-sendable — the redirect path clones for the same reason; this bug class is pinned by the #1036 MockClient test).
- **Observable, no new telemetry:** each retry fires the existing `transientRetryNotice` hook — the CLI host prints its dim `[net]` line + writes fa.log; hosts that leave the hook null (app host) stay silent, same as mid-stream retries today.
- **Exhaustion:** the same named watchdog `TimeoutException` rethrows unchanged → `formatProviderError` renders the `TimeoutException:` keyword → the roles/queue classifiers fail over exactly as today; a hard-down endpoint still dies loudly.
- **Mid-stream unchanged (AC3):** idle-timeout silence fires downstream in `createSseIterator` and never re-enters this layer — byte-identical path, pinned by test.
- **User abort:** the retry sleeper races the cancel token; a cancel during backoff propagates the abort (E4).

## Bench incident class coverage

The exact incident shape — first provider request stalled into the watchdog → run death — now survives up to 2 transparent retries with a visible note; a recovering endpoint answers on attempt 2/3 and the task proceeds. # pr-1125: fix(#1121): transparent bounded retry on zero-byte connect-stall watchdog timeout

## Description

Fixes #1121

## Root cause

`httpClient.send` completes only when the response **headers** arrive, so the connect watchdog's `TimeoutException` in `_sendWatched` (lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart) means **zero response bytes** — the provider never started generating. That exception escalated straight to the adapter's error event → run aborted. Bench run 36742787166 (glm-5.3-flash) lost 3/38 tasks this way (`gpt2-codegolf`, `polyglot-rust-c`, `write-compressor`): first request stalled on connect, watchdog fired at ~171s, `aborted: Request was aborted`, task scored failed with the prompt never sent.

## Retry semantics

- **Where:** `_sendWatched` — the single choke point all streaming adapters route through (`startProviderResponse` → `sendProviderRequest`). A connect-watchdog `TimeoutException` is retried **in place**, below the roles failover ladder and below `TransientRetryStream`.
- **Budget:** `providerConnectRetries = 2` (3 total attempts), backoff `providerConnectRetryBackoff` doubling 1s → 2s. Worst case ≈ 3×(180s+backoff) ≈ 10 min — the unattended/bench tradeoff priced in the issue (E1). Separate budget: a network stall never consumes a `retriesPerEntry` failover attempt (#1066 semantics) and never burns a `TransientRetryStream` attempt.
- **Safety:** zero bytes received ⇒ no partial stream to corrupt, no committed state, nothing double-billed (a request the endpoint never answered is not a billed generation) — the identical payload is simply re-sent. Retries ride a fresh `http.Request` clone via the existing `_reissue` helper (a sent Request is finalized by the client and not re-sendable — the redirect path clones for the same reason; this bug class is pinned by the #1036 MockClient test).
- **Observable, no new telemetry:** each retry fires the existing `transientRetryNotice` hook — the CLI host prints its dim `[net]` line + writes fa.log; hosts that leave the hook null (app host) stay silent, same as mid-stream retries today.
- **Exhaustion:** the same named watchdog `TimeoutException` rethrows unchanged → `formatProviderError` renders the `TimeoutException:` keyword → the roles/queue classifiers fail over exactly as today; a hard-down endpoint still dies loudly.
- **Mid-stream unchanged (AC3):** idle-timeout silence fires downstream in `createSseIterator` and never re-enters this layer — byte-identical path, pinned by test.
- **User abort:** the retry sleeper races the cancel token; a cancel during backoff propagates the abort (E4).

## Bench incident class coverage

The exact incident shape — first provider request stalled into the watchdog → run death — now survives up to 2 transparent retries with a visible note; a recovering endpoint answers on attempt 2/3 and the task proceeds. UT-1/UT-2/UT-3 (issue ACs) covered in `test/providers/connect_stall_retry_test.dart` (fake stream, 20ms watchdog, injectable sleeper): retry-to-success, exhaust→same error, mid-stream NOT retried, cancel-mid-backoff, happy path untouched. Scoped analyze clean; `test/providers` + `test/model_roles` suites green (722 tests).

Built on ai/gh-1036 (#1108, approved) — merged into this branch because #1036 review-round-2 reshaped `_sendWatched` itself; no conflict when that lands.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap

Interesting details in `chatgpt_codex.dart`:

1. `_consumeSseLines` — no `cancelToken` wiring into the stream itself: cancel during silence is only noticed at the next line or at idle timeout. `createSseIterator` DOES wire the cancel token (abandon + cancel immediately). So codex loses prompt-cancel latency during silence: a user abort during a silent codex stream waits up to `streamIdle` (5 min default) to take effect. Pre-existing? Before this PR: `await for (... ) { cancelToken?.throwIfCancelled(); ... }` — same delayed-cancel behavior (only checks between lines). And there was no watchdog at all, so a hang was forever. So not a regression — but now that they built the consumption loop, they could wire the cancelToken like createSseIterator does. It's a parity gap: createSseIterator supports cancelToken natively; `_consumeSseLines` reimplements a degraded version. SUGGESTION-level.

2. `_request` — the timeout on `client.send` — the 401-refresh loop and Cloudflare loop re-request; each gets its own 180s connect budget. Fine.

3. Note: in `run()`, after `_consumeSseLines`, `_sse.finish(_handleEvent)` etc. If `_consumeSseLines` throws TimeoutException, it propagates out of run() — presumably caught by the adapter's try/catch turning into ErrorEvent. The test confirms ErrorEvent. Good.

4. Codex connect watchdog: uses `effectiveProviderConnectTimeout` (streaming budget, 180s) — consistent with _sendWatched. BUT — no retry for codex! The #1121 retry only applies to `_sendWatched` (sendProviderRequest). Codex has its own `_request` path (bypasses sendProviderRequest) — so codex's connect stall does NOT retry. Is codex supposed to be covered by #1121? The issue says bench run lost 3/38 tasks — glm-5.3-flash — that routes through the standard adapters (openai-like), not codex. The retry is placed in `_sendWatched` "the single choke point all streaming adapters route through" — but codex does NOT route through it (has own client.send). # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1125
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1125
- **Title**: fix(#1121): transparent bounded retry on zero-byte connect-stall watchdog timeout
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1121` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +1023
- **Deletions**: -37
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T20:11:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T20:13:48Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1121

## Root cause

`httpClient.send` completes only when the response **headers** arrive, so the connect watchdog's `TimeoutException` in `_sendWatched` (lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart) means **zero response bytes** — the provider never started generating. That exception escalated straight to the adapter's error event → run aborted. Bench run 36742787166 (glm-5.3-flash) lost 3/38 tasks this way (`gpt2-codegolf`, `polyglot-rust-c`, `write-compressor`): first request stalled on connect, watchdog fired at ~171s, `aborted: Request was aborted`, task scored failed with the prompt never sent.

## Retry semantics

- **Where:** `_sendWatched` — the single choke point all streaming adapters route through (`startProviderResponse` → `sendProviderRequest`). A connect-watchdog `TimeoutException` is retried **in place**, below the roles failover ladder and below `TransientRetryStream`.
- **Budget:** `providerConnectRetries = 2` (3 total attempts), backoff `providerConnectRetryBackoff` doubling 1s → 2s. Worst case ≈ 3×(180s+backoff) ≈ 10 min — the unattended/bench tradeoff priced in the issue (E1). Separate budget: a network stall never consumes a `retriesPerEntry` failover attempt (#1066 semantics) and never burns a `TransientRetryStream` attempt.
- **Safety:** zero bytes received ⇒ no partial stream to corrupt, no committed state, nothing double-billed (a request the endpoint never answered is not a billed generation) — the identical payload is simply re-sent. Retries ride a fresh `http.Request` clone via the existing `_reissue` helper (a sent Request is finalized by the client and not re-sendable — the redirect path clones for the same reason; this bug class is pinned by the #1036 MockClient test).
- **Observable, no new telemetry:** each retry fires the existing `transientRetryNotice` hook — the CLI host prints its dim `[net]` line + writes fa.log; hosts that leave the hook null (app host) stay silent, same as mid-stream retries today.
- **Exhaustion:** the same named watchdog `TimeoutException` rethrows unchanged → `formatProviderError` renders the `TimeoutException:` keyword → the roles/queue classifiers fail over exactly as today; a hard-down endpoint still dies loudly.
- **Mid-stream unchanged (AC3):** idle-timeout silence fires downstream in `createSseIterator` and never re-enters this layer — byte-identical path, pinned by test.
- **User abort:** the retry sleeper races the cancel token; a cancel during backoff propagates the abort (E4).

## Bench incident class coverage

The exact incident shape — first provider request stalled into the watchdog → run death — now survives up to 2 transparent retries with a visible note; a recovering endpoint answers on attempt 2/3 and the task proceeds. UT-1/UT-2/UT-3 (issue ACs) covered in `test/providers/connect_stall_retry_test.dart` (fake stream, 20ms watchdog, injectable sleeper): retry-to-success, exhaust→same error, mid-stream NOT retried, cancel-mid-backoff, happy path untouched. Scoped analyze clean; `test/providers` + `test/model_roles` suites green (722 tests).

Built on ai/gh-1036 (#1108, approved) — merged into this branch because #1036 review-round-2 reshaped `_sendWatched` itself; no conflict when that lands.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
